_doc: HMTc Category 11 (Meat, Poultry, and Eggs) compiler config. Method v2.0, government-limit-only initial setting. Nine rows: beef, pork, lamb/mutton, poultry, game, eggs, processed meats, canned meats, and plant-based meat alternatives. THE INSTRUMENT PICTURE FOR THIS CATEGORY IS ASYMMETRIC AND THE CONFIG IS BUILT AROUND THAT FACT. EU Regulation (EU) 2023/915 supplies the cadmium maximum level for muscle meat of bovine animals, sheep, pig and poultry (50 ug/kg) and FSANZ Schedule 19 supplies a lead maximum level for the same species set (100 ug/kg), but neither instrument sets terrestrial-animal maximum levels for arsenic, mercury or chromium, and the EU and Codex lead rows for meat are ABSENT FROM THIS REGISTER (recorded as register gaps, not invented). Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 is the only credible sovereign instrument on the register with a complete per-commodity panel for terrestrial animal foods, and it therefore anchors the arsenic, mercury and chromium cells across the category and the lead and mercury cells for eggs. Hong Kong was admitted to the HMTc credible-regulator set on 2026-08-17 (the Category 35 bone-broth precedent) for exactly this reason. MUSCLE MEAT AND OFFAL ARE DIFFERENT SCOPES: every row is scoped to muscle meat and attached edible fat, offal is a separately-tested sub-lot governed by its own species' offal maximum levels, and no offal value is permitted to anchor a muscle-meat row anywhere in this config. Canned meats additionally carry the canned-foods tin maximum level (EU 2023/915 binds at 200 mg/kg over the 250 mg/kg of Codex, FSANZ and Hong Kong); every other row treats tin as a control because the tinplate pathway is absent. Plant-based meat alternatives are a composite of pulse, soy and cereal protein components and use component_read_across throughout, which is also the only row where nickel is a numeric cell rather than a control. Nickel and aluminium are controls on all animal rows because every credible nickel and aluminium value on the register is a plant-matrix maximum level, a drinking-water statutory limit, a migration limit or an infant-formula maximum level, none of which can govern animal muscle tissue. Inorganic arsenic is a CONTROL rather than a not-material determination across every row: organoarsenical feed additives were historically administered to poultry and swine, and rice protein is a common extender in meat analogues, so the affirmative claim that no inorganic-arsenic pathway exists is one this programme will not make. Methylmercury and hexavalent chromium are the two substantiated not-material cells, both speciation-bounded by their published total-element parents. Numbers are NEVER occurrence-derived. Allowed provenance tags: regulatory-alignment, read-across, not-material, control, ratchet. STAFF/HMTc content, not public wiki (CLAUDE.md Part 19 firewall).

_category.name: Meat, Poultry, and Eggs
_category.anchor: per-commodity sovereign metallic-contamination schedules for terrestrial animal foods — Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 Schedule (the only credible instrument on the register with a complete meat, poultry and egg panel), EU Regulation (EU) 2023/915 for cadmium in muscle meat, and FSANZ Schedule 19 for lead in muscle meat; canned forms additionally carry the canned-foods tin maximum level, and the plant-protein analogue row reads across from EU and Hong Kong pulse, soy and cereal commodity maximum levels
_category.basis_family: dietary as-sold, edible portion, wet weight (bone, shell and inedible fat excluded); no reconstitution, drained-weight or dry-to-wet conversion is performed anywhere in this category — the 8:1 powder-to-liquid conversion is confined to infant formula
_category.method_label: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only initial setting: the strictest applicable sovereign maximum level for this exact product form in its native basis; disclosed read-across where the exact cell is unregulated; control where neither a sovereign number nor a supportable near-neighbour analogue exists; never occurrence-derived)
_category.method_note: Category-specific method notes. (1) MUSCLE MEAT vs OFFAL. Every credible instrument writes separate and materially looser maximum levels for edible offal, because lead and cadmium concentrate in liver and kidney. Every row here is scoped to muscle meat and attached edible fat; offal of the same species is a separately-tested sub-lot assessed against that species' offal maximum levels, and no offal value anchors a muscle-meat row. The taxonomy boundary rule places offal inside the animal's own subcategory, which is honoured by sub-lot testing rather than by publishing an offal-derived ceiling. (2) THE CATEGORY 1 BOUNDARY. Products marketed for ages 0-5 route to Category 1 (mixed meals), so the infant and baby-food action levels and maximum levels that would otherwise be the strictest values in the register are excluded by applicability from every row here, and are excluded explicitly in each row's audit_exclude_scope. (3) GAME AND LEAD AMMUNITION. Fragmenting lead projectiles are a documented, mechanical lead pathway in wild-harvested game. That evidence drives mandatory radiographic fragment screening before grinding and priority surveillance on the game row; it does not and cannot move the number, which remains a disclosed read-across from the domestic-mammal muscle-meat maximum level. (4) BASIS TREATMENT ON THE THREE COMPOSITE ROWS, DISCLOSED IN THE DIRECTION IT CUTS. On the processed-meat, canned-meat and analogue rows the component maximum level is applied to the finished product as sold, with no invented conversion factor. This config does NOT claim that treatment is conservative, because it is not: a formulation that is part water, brine, starch or rusk can carry a higher concentration in its meat or protein fraction than the component maximum level itself allows. The gap is closed by a second, independent obligation rather than by a conversion factor. Certification of those three rows requires documented compliance of the raw material or source commodity against the same named component maximum levels, in their own basis, IN ADDITION to finished-product compliance against the published ceiling; neither test substitutes for the other. The eggs row runs the opposite way and is treated accordingly: dried and powdered egg is concentrated relative to whole egg, so applying the whole-egg maximum level to the powder as sold is the STRICTER treatment, and it is applied without being reversed. (5) REGISTER GAPS ARE DISCLOSED, NOT FILLED. The EU 2023/915 and Codex CXS 193 lead rows for meat and offal, the EU and Codex cadmium offal rows, and the FSANZ cadmium meat and offal rows are absent from this register. They are recorded as register gaps for ingestion through the verified regulatory-fetch pathway and are NOT written into this config from memory. No absent row is assigned a remembered value anywhere in this config. Because the method selects the strictest applicable value, ingesting a missing row can only lower a published cell or leave it unchanged, never raise it; every affected cell must be re-derived when the missing rows land.

beef-product.name: Beef
beef-product.native_basis_label: as sold, raw or cooked edible portion (wet weight); bone and inedible fat excluded; no dry-to-wet or reconstitution conversion is performed
beef-product.scope_note: Muscle meat and attached edible fat of cattle (Bos taurus, Bos indicus) in every retail and foodservice form: fresh, chilled, frozen, vacuum- and modified-atmosphere-packed, ground/minced, primal and sub-primal cuts, and plain cooked or sous-vide beef with no added non-meat ingredients. Bovine edible offal (liver, kidney, heart, tongue, tripe) is IN the category by the taxonomy boundary rule but is a separately-tested sub-lot assessed against the sovereign bovine-offal maximum levels; the offal values must never anchor this muscle-meat row and are not published as this row's ceiling. Cured, smoked, fermented, comminuted or otherwise formulated beef products (corned beef, pastrami, beef sausage, jerky with added ingredients) route to the processed-meats row; canned beef routes to the canned-meats row; beef marketed for ages 0-5 routes to Category 1 (mixed meals). Bison and other non-domestic bovids route to the game-meats row.

beef-product.audit_exclude_scope: infant|baby|toddler|young child|follow.?on|follow.?up|formula|weaning|complementary food|under the age of 36 months|persons under the age|children under 2|fish|crustacean|mollusc|bivalve|cephalopod|oyster|prawn|shrimp|crab|tuna|aquatic|seafood|seaweed|offal|liver|kidney|blood|feed|pet food
beef-product.basis_guard: (wet weight|portion ordinarily consumed|product as placed on market|food as listed|as sold|as consumed|commodity|edible part|fresh weight)
beef-product.basis_guard_note: Category 11 is a dietary as-sold wet-weight category. The guard admits only register rows whose basis is a food-matrix content basis (wet weight, portion ordinarily consumed, product as placed on market, commodity, edible part, food as listed in the Cap 132V schedule). It rejects, by construction, food-contact specific-migration limits, toy and article element-migration limits, animal-feed 12%-moisture bases, dry-matter fertiliser limits, colour-additive ingredient purity specifications, and drinking-water statutory limits. A migration or purity-specification number is not a maximum level for a food and must never anchor a meat, poultry, or egg row.

Pb.label: strictest applicable sovereign muscle-meat lead maximum level; FSANZ Schedule 19 and Hong Kong Cap. 132V agree at 100 ug/kg
Pb.substantiation: Two credible sovereign instruments regulate this exact cell and agree: FSANZ Australia New Zealand Food Standards Code Schedule 19 sets 0.1 mg/kg for meat of cattle, sheep, pig and poultry excluding offal, and Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 sets 0.1 mg/kg for meat of cattle, pig, goat and sheep. The corresponding EU Regulation (EU) 2023/915 and Codex CXS 193-1995 muscle-meat lead rows are ABSENT from this register and are therefore not named and not assigned a value from memory; they are recorded as register gaps for ingestion through the verified regulatory-fetch pathway. Because Method v2.0 selects the strictest applicable value, ingesting them can only lower this cell or leave it unchanged, never raise it, and this cell must be re-derived when they land. The looser edible-offal lead maximum levels (Hong Kong 0.15-0.20 mg/kg, FSANZ 0.5 mg/kg) are a DIFFERENT product scope and are deliberately not used to anchor this muscle-meat row: Bovine offal is a separately-tested sub-lot governed by the offal maximum levels of its own species.

Cd.label: strictest applicable sovereign muscle-meat cadmium maximum level; EU 2023/915 and Hong Kong Cap. 132V agree at 50 ug/kg
Cd.substantiation: EU Regulation (EU) 2023/915 Annex I sets 0.050 mg/kg cadmium for meat of bovine animals, sheep, pig and poultry, expressly excluding offal, and Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 sets the same 0.05 mg/kg for meat of cattle, pigs, goat and sheep. Cadmium concentrates in liver and kidney, and the sovereign liver (0.5 mg/kg) and kidney (1.0 mg/kg) maximum levels are an order of magnitude looser; they govern offal sub-lots and are deliberately not permitted to anchor this muscle-meat row.

tAs.label: Hong Kong Cap. 132V total-arsenic maximum level for meat of animal
tAs.substantiation: Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 Schedule sets 0.5 mg/kg arsenic (expressed as total arsenic) for meat of animal, the edible portion after removal of bone. Hong Kong was admitted to the HMTc credible-regulator set on 2026-08-17 precisely because its per-commodity metallic-contamination schedule covers terrestrial-animal commodities that the EU, Codex and FSANZ leave open. No credible sovereign government sets a stricter total-arsenic maximum level for terrestrial muscle meat. The toxic inorganic fraction is separately controlled under the iAs cell, which is a control with reflex speciation rather than a not-material determination.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets an inorganic-arsenic maximum level for terrestrial red-meat muscle tissue. Every credible inorganic-arsenic instrument on the register is scoped elsewhere: EU 2023/915 and EU 2025/1891 to rice, rice products, fruit juices, infant food and seafood; UK, Health Canada and US FDA to rice-based and juice matrices; Hong Kong Cap. 132V to rice and aquatic animals. A NOT-MATERIAL determination is deliberately REJECTED for this cell rather than adopted for convenience: organoarsenical feed additives (roxarsone, nitarsone, arsanilic acid, carbarsone) were lawfully administered to poultry and swine in major producing markets within living memory and are documented to leave arsenic residues in edible tissue, so the programme will not make the affirmative claim that no inorganic-arsenic pathway exists in terrestrial animal food. For the ruminant rows, where no equivalent additive history applies, the absence of that pathway does not by itself substantiate a not-material determination either, because neither a sovereign number nor a supportable near-neighbour analogue exists for the cell in any case. Because no sovereign number governs the cell and no near-neighbour cell is a supportable analogue (a rice or seafood inorganic-arsenic maximum level describes a different contamination mechanism entirely), the cell is a control: testing is mandatory and no ceiling is invented.
control.reference_method: Inorganic arsenic by anion-exchange HPLC-ICP-MS speciation. Speciation is reflex-triggered on every lot whose total-arsenic screen is quantifiable above the method limit of quantitation, and unconditionally on the first lot from any new supplier, slaughter establishment, or country of origin. Any quantifiable inorganic arsenic is escalated to the certification committee together with the feed-additive and origin declaration; the lot cannot be released on an inorganic-arsenic result while the escalation is open, and a total-arsenic result at or above the binding total-arsenic maximum level is a hard stop irrespective of speciation.

tHg.label: Hong Kong Cap. 132V total-mercury maximum level for meat of animal
tHg.substantiation: Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 item for mercury (expressed as total mercury), meat of animal, 0.05 mg/kg = 50 ug/kg. This is the same instrument and the same row that anchors the Category 35 bone-broth mercury cell, adopted on the 2026-08-17 credible-set ruling. The EU, Codex and FSANZ set mercury maximum levels only for fish and seafood, so Hong Kong supplies the only credible terrestrial-animal mercury ceiling and it binds directly rather than by read-across.

not_material.rationale: Methylmercury is formed by microbial methylation in aquatic sediment and biomagnifies through aquatic food webs. Terrestrial red meat carries no methylation pathway and no aquatic trophic transfer, and methylmercury is in any event a component of total mercury (MeHg <= tHg), so it is bounded by and controlled through the published total-mercury cell (50 ug/kg total mercury, Hong Kong Cap. 132V). No separate methylmercury ceiling is published because none would bind below the total-mercury ceiling and none is set by any credible sovereign government for this product form.
not_material.reference_method: Not measured routinely. Bounded by the total-mercury cell; methylmercury speciation by HPLC-ICP-MS is reflex-triggered only where a lot's total-mercury result approaches the binding total-mercury maximum level, or where the formulation incorporates a fish, fish-meal, or marine-derived ingredient, which would additionally route the lot to the Category 6 seafood mercury ceilings.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign government sets a methylmercury content limit for meat, poultry, game, eggs, or meat analogues. The credible methylmercury instruments (EU 2023/915 Annex I section 3.3, US FDA CPG 540.600, FSANZ Schedule 19, Hong Kong Cap. 132V) are scoped exclusively to fish, crustaceans, molluscs and other aquatic animals. Methylmercury is a species of, and arithmetically bounded by, total mercury.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU (Regulation (EU) 2023/915 Annex I); UK retained contaminants law; Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA (CPG 540.600); FSANZ Australia New Zealand Food Standards Code Schedule 19; Health Canada; Hong Kong Cap. 132V Food Adulteration (Metallic Contamination) Regulations Part 2 Schedule — none sets a methylmercury limit for a terrestrial animal food, an egg, or a plant-protein meat analogue.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a nickel maximum level for meat of cattle, pig, goat, sheep or any other terrestrial mammal. The EU nickel maximum levels recorded on the register (the eu2024_ni_* family) are drawn exclusively over plant matrices — cereals, pulses, legume, leafy and root vegetables, tree nuts, oilseeds, cocoa — and the only other credible nickel values are drinking-water statutory limits and a food-contact specific-migration limit, both in bases that cannot govern the content of a food. A plant-commodity nickel maximum level is not a supportable near-neighbour for animal muscle tissue, which accumulates nickel by a different route and at a different order of magnitude, so no read-across is available and no ceiling is invented.
control.reference_method: Total nickel by ICP-MS on every certified lot, trended per SKU and per production line. Escalation is triggered by a result above the SKU's established rolling upper control limit, or by an increasing trend across three consecutive lots, and directs the investigation to nickel-bearing stainless contact surfaces (grinders, mincers, brine injectors, forming plates). No numeric ceiling is published because no sovereign instrument compels one.

control.rationale: Inorganic tin in food is a tinplate-packaging pathway: tin migrates into the food from the internal surface of an unlacquered or damaged tinplate can, which is why every credible sovereign tin maximum level on the register is written against canned food rather than against the food itself. Fresh, chilled, frozen and vacuum- or modified-atmosphere-packed red meat is not packed in tinplate, so the pathway that the canned-food maximum levels exist to control is absent and no sovereign number governs the cell. A lot of this product form that is retorted or packed in a metal can is not certified against this row at all: it is certified against the canned-meats row, whose tin cell carries the binding canned-foods maximum level. No tin ceiling is invented for the non-canned form.
control.reference_method: Total tin by ICP-MS on every certified lot. Any quantifiable tin in a lot declared as non-metal-packed triggers a packaging and contact-surface investigation (can or closure liner, tinned equipment, solder) before release, and re-routes the lot to the canned-meats row if metal packaging is found.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets an aluminium maximum level for meat, poultry, game or eggs. The credible aluminium values on the register are drinking- and bottled-water statutory limits (EU 2020/2184, US FDA 21 CFR 165.110, Health Canada), a food-contact specific-migration limit (EU 10/2011), toy element-migration limits, and the FSANZ Schedule 19 aluminium maximum levels for infant formula. None can anchor this row: the water and migration values are in a different basis, and an adult food must not borrow an infant-formula maximum level (products marketed for ages 0-5 route to Category 1 by the taxonomy boundary rule). No read-across is supportable and no ceiling is invented.
control.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, trended per SKU. Escalation is triggered by a result above the SKU's established rolling upper control limit or by an increasing trend across three consecutive lots, and directs the investigation to aluminium contact surfaces and packaging (foil, trays, aluminium cookware, aluminium-containing processing aids). No numeric ceiling is published because no sovereign instrument compels one.

Cr.screen_note: Total chromium in food is dominated by benign trivalent chromium, an essential trace element; the health-relevant species is hexavalent chromium, which does not persist in this matrix (see the Cr-VI cell). The Hong Kong Cap. 132V total-chromium maximum level is a real sovereign limit and is published here, but it is recorded as a SCREEN: it is a contact-surface and equipment-leaching tripwire, not a standalone protective ceiling, and it is excluded from the firm-limit count.
Cr.label: Hong Kong Cap. 132V total-chromium maximum level for meat of animal, published as a screen
Cr.substantiation: Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 Schedule sets 1 mg/kg chromium for meat of animal. It is the only credible sovereign total-chromium value for a terrestrial-animal food and is adopted at face value, but recorded as a screen because total chromium is not the health-relevant analyte: the toxic species is Cr(VI), which does not persist in a reducing protein matrix (see the Cr-VI cell).

not_material.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is not stable in this matrix. Raw and cooked red-meat muscle tissue is a wet, reducing, protein- and thiol-rich medium; Cr(VI) is reduced to Cr(III) by tissue reductants (cysteine, glutathione, ascorbate) and by the acid and heat of digestion and cooking, so a Cr(VI) figure reported on such a matrix is an artifact of the extraction chemistry of the total-chromium screen rather than a measurement of a species that persists in the food. The determination follows the same reference-method adjudication recorded for the hexavalent-chromium cell in the infant-formula category (data/workbench standards Cr-VI adjudication), applied here to an animal-tissue matrix. Hexavalent chromium is in any event a species of, and bounded by, the published total-chromium screen (Cr-VI <= total Cr).
not_material.reference_method: Not measured routinely. Bounded by the total-chromium screen (Cr cell). Alkaline-extraction Cr(VI) determination (IC-ICP-MS) is reflex-triggered only where the total-chromium screen exceeds the published screen value, in which case the investigation is directed at stainless-steel contact surfaces, grinders, and brine or marinade equipment rather than at the raw material.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign government sets a hexavalent-chromium content limit for any food. Every credible Cr(VI) instrument on the register is an article, textile, leather, toy-migration, tattoo-ink, fertiliser or electrical-equipment limit in a non-food basis, and applying one to a food matrix would be a basis conflation the compiler's basis guard rejects. Total chromium is regulated for meat and poultry by Hong Kong Cap. 132V and is published here as a screen.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU (Regulation (EU) 2023/915; Regulation (EU) 10/2011; Directive 2009/48/EC; REACH restrictions); UK; Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA; FSANZ Schedule 19; Health Canada; Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 Schedule — none sets a hexavalent-chromium content limit for food.

Sn.label: strictest applicable sovereign canned-food tin maximum level; EU Regulation (EU) 2023/915 binds at 200000 ug/kg (200 mg/kg) against 250 mg/kg in Codex CXS 193, FSANZ Schedule 19 and Hong Kong Cap. 132V
Sn.basis_label: as sold, whole can contents as packed (wet weight)
Sn.substantiation: Four credible sovereign instruments regulate tin in canned food other than canned beverages: EU Regulation (EU) 2023/915 at 200 mg/kg, Codex CXS 193-1995 at 250 mg/kg, FSANZ Schedule 19 at 250 mg/kg, and Hong Kong Cap. 132V at 250 mg/kg. All four are named so the selection is auditable, and the strictest applicable value binds: 200 mg/kg = 200000 ug/kg. The canned-BEVERAGE tin maximum levels (EU 100 mg/kg, Hong Kong 150 mg/kg) are stricter but are a different product form and are not applicable to a canned meat; the canned infant-food and canned-infant-formula tin maximum levels (50 mg/kg, EU and UK) are stricter still but are infant scopes, and products marketed for ages 0-5 route to Category 1 by the taxonomy boundary rule. The superseded pre-2019 Hong Kong all-food entry is gated out by its register status.

plant-based-meat-alternatives.name: Plant-based meat alternatives (burgers, sausages, nuggets; pea/soy/wheat-protein base)
plant-based-meat-alternatives.native_basis_label: as sold, finished formulated product (wet weight for chilled and frozen forms, product as placed on market for dry mixes); dry-commodity component maximum levels are applied to the hydrated finished product with no dry-to-wet conversion, which is the looser of the two available treatments and is disclosed as such, so certification additionally requires documented source-commodity compliance for every protein ingredient
plant-based-meat-alternatives.scope_note: Formulated meat analogues whose protein is wholly plant-derived: pea- and other pulse-protein isolates and concentrates, soy protein isolate, concentrate and textured soy protein, and wheat gluten/seitan, sold as burgers, patties, sausages, nuggets, grounds, strips and deli-style slices. Fungal-biomass (mycoprotein) and precision-fermentation products route to Category 29; dairy- and egg-based analogues route to their own categories; a blended meat-and-plant product is certified on the processed-meats row against the stricter of the two rows' applicable values, cell by cell. Any formulation incorporating rice or rice protein additionally carries the sovereign rice inorganic-arsenic maximum level, which is named as the companion instrument in the iAs cell.
plant-based-meat-alternatives.audit_exclude_scope: infant|baby|toddler|young child|follow.?on|follow.?up|formula|weaning|complementary food|under the age of 36 months|persons under the age|children under 2|fish|crustacean|mollusc|bivalve|cephalopod|oyster|prawn|shrimp|crab|tuna|aquatic|seafood|seaweed|feed|pet food
plant-based-meat-alternatives.basis_guard: (wet weight|portion ordinarily consumed|product as placed on market|food as listed|as sold|as consumed|commodity|edible part|fresh weight)
plant-based-meat-alternatives.basis_guard_note: Category 11 is a dietary as-sold wet-weight category. The guard admits only register rows whose basis is a food-matrix content basis (wet weight, portion ordinarily consumed, product as placed on market, commodity, edible part, food as listed in the Cap 132V schedule). It rejects, by construction, food-contact specific-migration limits, toy and article element-migration limits, animal-feed 12%-moisture bases, dry-matter fertiliser limits, colour-additive ingredient purity specifications, and drinking-water statutory limits. A migration or purity-specification number is not a maximum level for a food and must never anchor a meat, poultry, or egg row.

components.component: pulses (pea and other pulse protein source commodity)

component_read_across.label: strictest applicable principal-component lead maximum level; the pulse and legume-vegetable rows bind at 100 ug/kg over the looser cereal row at 200 ug/kg
component_read_across.substantiation: No credible sovereign government sets a lead maximum level for a meat analogue, so the exact cell is unregulated and the ceiling reads across from the maximum levels governing the principal protein components. Hong Kong Cap. 132V sets 0.1 mg/kg for pulses and 0.1 mg/kg for legume vegetables, the commodity classes from which pea and soy protein are drawn; FSANZ Schedule 19 sets 0.2 mg/kg for cereals, the class from which wheat gluten is drawn. The strictest applicable component value binds at 100 ug/kg, so a wheat-gluten-based analogue is held to the pulse ceiling rather than the looser cereal one. BASIS TREATMENT, DISCLOSED IN THE DIRECTION IT ACTUALLY CUTS: the component maximum levels are written on dry commodities as placed on the market and are applied to the hydrated finished product as sold, with no dry-to-wet conversion, because Method v2.0 forbids inventing a basis conversion. That is the LOOSER of the two available treatments, not a conservative one: a hydrated extrudate is mostly water, so a protein ingredient can exceed its own commodity maximum level and still leave the finished product inside this ceiling. The programme states that openly and closes the gap with a second, independent requirement rather than with a conversion factor: every certified lot must carry supplier documentation of the source commodity for each protein ingredient, tested against the named component maximum levels in the commodity own basis, in addition to finished-product compliance against this ceiling. The ingredient-basis treatment is the natural candidate for the first Standards Ratchet review on this row once eligible certified-lot data exist.

components.component: pulses (pea and other pulse protein source commodity)

component_read_across.label: strictest applicable principal-component cadmium maximum level; the EU pulses row binds at 40 ug/kg over soy beans at 200 and wheat gluten at 150
component_read_across.substantiation: EU Regulation (EU) 2023/915 Annex I sets cadmium maximum levels for each of this row's principal protein commodities: pulses 0.040 mg/kg, soy beans (with peanuts) 0.20 mg/kg, and wheat gluten (with rice, quinoa and wheat bran) 0.15 mg/kg. The strictest applicable component value binds at 40 ug/kg. This is the tightest cell in Category 11 and it is deliberately not relaxed toward the soy row: the method takes the strictest applicable component maximum level, and a soy-based analogue is not entitled to the looser oilseed ceiling merely because soy is the protein it happens to use.

components.component: cereals other than rice (wheat gluten source commodity)
cereal grains and milled cereal products (FSANZ)

component_read_across.label: strictest applicable principal-component total-arsenic maximum level; Hong Kong Cap. 132V cereals other than rice binds at 500 ug/kg over the FSANZ cereal-grain row at 1000
component_read_across.substantiation: No credible sovereign government sets a total-arsenic maximum level for pulses, peas, soy beans or a meat analogue. The nearest applicable component cells are the cereal rows that govern the wheat-gluten component: Hong Kong Cap. 132V cereals other than rice at 0.5 mg/kg and FSANZ Schedule 19 cereal grains and milled cereal products at 1.0 mg/kg. Both are named and the stricter binds at 500 ug/kg. Rice is deliberately excluded from the component set and from the audit scope: a rice-containing formulation is governed by the far more consequential sovereign rice INORGANIC-arsenic maximum levels, which are handled as the companion instrument in the iAs cell rather than folded into a total-arsenic average here.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets an inorganic-arsenic maximum level for pulses, peas, soy beans, wheat gluten or a plant-protein meat analogue. Every credible inorganic-arsenic instrument on the register is scoped to rice and rice products, fruit and vegetable juices, infant foods, or seafood. A not-material determination is REJECTED because a real and formulation-dependent inorganic-arsenic pathway exists in this row: rice protein and rice flour are common binders and protein extenders in meat analogues, and rice is the single most arsenic-accumulating food crop. The cell is therefore a control with a formulation-triggered reflex, and no ceiling is invented for the non-rice formulation.
control.reference_method: Inorganic arsenic by anion-exchange HPLC-ICP-MS speciation. Speciation is MANDATORY on every lot whose declared formulation contains rice, rice protein, rice flour, rice starch or rice syrup, and reflex-triggered on any other formulation whose total-arsenic screen is quantifiable above the method limit of quantitation. A rice-containing lot is additionally assessed against the sovereign rice inorganic-arsenic maximum level named as this cell's companion instrument, and the stricter applicable value binds.

components.component: wheat and wheat flour (wheat gluten source commodity)

component_read_across.label: read-across from the Hong Kong Cap. 132V total-mercury maximum level covering wheat and wheat flour (20 ug/kg), the only credible sovereign mercury value governing any principal component of this row
component_read_across.substantiation: Hong Kong Cap. 132V sets 0.02 mg/kg total mercury for rice, husked rice, polished rice, maize, maize flour, wheat and wheat flour. That row governs the cereal component from which wheat gluten is drawn and is the only credible sovereign mercury maximum level applicable to any principal component of a plant-protein analogue; no credible instrument sets a mercury value for pulses or soy beans. It binds at 20 ug/kg, which is stricter than the 50 ug/kg terrestrial-meat mercury ceiling elsewhere in this category. That asymmetry is a fact about the sovereign instruments and is disclosed, not harmonised: the method selects the strictest applicable component value and does not adjust a plant-matrix ceiling upward to match an animal-matrix one. The EU cereal mercury figure of 0.01 mg/kg was reviewed and NOT used because it is a pesticide maximum residue level, a different regulatory instrument in a different basis, and pesticide-residue instruments are excluded from contaminant anchoring.

not_material.rationale: Methylmercury is formed by microbial methylation in aquatic sediment and biomagnifies through aquatic food webs. A plant-protein meat analogue carries no methylation pathway and no aquatic trophic transfer, and methylmercury is in any event a component of total mercury (MeHg <= tHg), so it is bounded by and controlled through the published total-mercury cell (20 ug/kg total mercury, Hong Kong Cap. 132V wheat row). No separate methylmercury ceiling is published because none would bind below the total-mercury ceiling and none is set by any credible sovereign government for this product form.
not_material.reference_method: Not measured routinely. Bounded by the total-mercury cell; methylmercury speciation by HPLC-ICP-MS is reflex-triggered only where a lot's total-mercury result approaches the binding total-mercury maximum level, or where the formulation incorporates a fish, fish-meal, or marine-derived ingredient, which would additionally route the lot to the Category 6 seafood mercury ceilings.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign government sets a methylmercury content limit for meat, poultry, game, eggs, or meat analogues. The credible methylmercury instruments (EU 2023/915 Annex I section 3.3, US FDA CPG 540.600, FSANZ Schedule 19, Hong Kong Cap. 132V) are scoped exclusively to fish, crustaceans, molluscs and other aquatic animals. Methylmercury is a species of, and arithmetically bounded by, total mercury.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU (Regulation (EU) 2023/915 Annex I); UK retained contaminants law; Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA (CPG 540.600); FSANZ Australia New Zealand Food Standards Code Schedule 19; Health Canada; Hong Kong Cap. 132V Food Adulteration (Metallic Contamination) Regulations Part 2 Schedule — none sets a methylmercury limit for a terrestrial animal food, an egg, or a plant-protein meat analogue.

components.component: pulses (pea and other pulse protein source commodity)
soy beans / edamame (soy protein source commodity)

component_read_across.label: strictest applicable principal-component nickel maximum level; the EU cereals row binds at 800 ug/kg over legume vegetables 1000, pulses 4000 and soy beans 6000
component_read_across.substantiation: This is the one row in Category 11 where nickel is NOT a control, because the EU nickel maximum levels are drawn over exactly the plant commodities this row is formulated from. All four applicable component rows are named and disclosed: cereals 0.8 mg/kg, legume vegetables 1.0 mg/kg, pulses 4.0 mg/kg, soy beans and edamame 6.0 mg/kg. The strictest applicable component value binds at 800 ug/kg. Nickel matters here in a way it does not for muscle meat: pulses and soy are genuine nickel accumulators, and catalytic hydrogenation of plant fats is a nickel pathway, so a plant-protein analogue is the form in which a nickel ceiling is both available and warranted. The looser soy-bean oilseed row (15 mg/kg) and dry-bean row (12 mg/kg) were reviewed and not adopted: they describe whole oilseed and dry pulse commodities rather than the protein fraction used here, and adopting them would loosen the ceiling by an order of magnitude for no instrument-compelled reason.

control.rationale: Inorganic tin in food is a tinplate-packaging pathway: tin migrates into the food from the internal surface of an unlacquered or damaged tinplate can, which is why every credible sovereign tin maximum level on the register is written against canned food rather than against the food itself. A chilled, frozen or film-packed plant-protein meat analogue is not packed in tinplate, so the pathway that the canned-food maximum levels exist to control is absent and no sovereign number governs the cell. A lot of this product form that is retorted or packed in a metal can is not certified against this row at all: it is certified against the canned-meats row, whose tin cell carries the binding canned-foods maximum level. No tin ceiling is invented for the non-canned form.
control.reference_method: Total tin by ICP-MS on every certified lot. Any quantifiable tin in a lot declared as non-metal-packed triggers a packaging and contact-surface investigation (can or closure liner, tinned equipment, solder) before release, and re-routes the lot to the canned-meats row if metal packaging is found.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets an aluminium maximum level for pulses, soy, wheat gluten or a plant-protein meat analogue. The credible aluminium values on the register are drinking- and bottled-water statutory limits, a food-contact specific-migration limit, toy element-migration limits, and the FSANZ infant-formula maximum levels; none can anchor this row, and an adult food must not borrow an infant-formula value. No read-across is supportable and no ceiling is invented. Aluminium nonetheless warrants a named control on this row specifically, because aluminium-containing acidity regulators, firming agents and anti-caking agents are permitted in formulated plant products and because protein isolation uses aluminium-bearing processing equipment.
control.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, trended per SKU and per protein-isolate supplier. Escalation is triggered by a result above the SKU's established rolling upper control limit or by an increasing trend across three consecutive lots, and directs the investigation to declared aluminium-containing additives and processing aids, to the isolate supplier's extraction chemistry, and to aluminium contact surfaces and packaging. No numeric ceiling is published because no sovereign instrument compels one.

read_across.label: read-across from the Hong Kong Cap. 132V total-chromium maximum level for pulses (1000 ug/kg), published as a screen; the cereals entry in the same instrument carries the identical value
read_across.substantiation: No credible sovereign government sets a total-chromium maximum level for a meat analogue. Hong Kong Cap. 132V sets 1 mg/kg for pulses and 1 mg/kg for cereals, the two principal component commodity classes; the pulses row is named and the cereals row is disclosed at the same value, so the binding number is unaffected by which component dominates the formulation. Published as a screen because total chromium is dominated by trivalent chromium and is not the health-relevant analyte; the screen functions here as an extruder and stainless-contact tripwire, high-moisture extrusion being the defining unit operation of this product form. Hong Kong's stricter row for vegetables other than pulses (0.5 mg/kg) was reviewed and not adopted: minor vegetable, starch and hydrocolloid ingredients are not principal protein components of this row, and a lot whose formulation is principally vegetable rather than pulse, soy or cereal protein is routed to the vegetable rows in Categories 27 and 28 instead.

Cr.screen_note: Total chromium in food is dominated by benign trivalent chromium, an essential trace element; the health-relevant species is hexavalent chromium, which does not persist in this matrix (see the Cr-VI cell). The Hong Kong Cap. 132V total-chromium maximum level is a real sovereign limit and is published here, but it is recorded as a SCREEN: it is a contact-surface and equipment-leaching tripwire, not a standalone protective ceiling, and it is excluded from the firm-limit count.

not_material.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is not stable in this matrix. A hydrated, cooked, high-protein extrudate is a reducing medium; Cr(VI) is reduced to Cr(III) by plant-matrix reductants (ascorbate, phenolics, thiols) and by the heat and shear of high-moisture extrusion, so a Cr(VI) figure reported on such a matrix is an artifact of the extraction chemistry of the total-chromium screen rather than a measurement of a species that persists in the food. The determination follows the reference-method adjudication recorded for the hexavalent-chromium cell in the infant-formula category, applied here to a plant-protein extrudate. Hexavalent chromium is in any event a species of, and bounded by, the published total-chromium screen (Cr-VI <= total Cr).
not_material.reference_method: Not measured routinely. Bounded by the total-chromium screen (Cr cell). Alkaline-extraction Cr(VI) determination (IC-ICP-MS) is reflex-triggered only where the total-chromium screen exceeds the published screen value, in which case the investigation is directed at the extruder barrel, screws and die and at stainless slurry-handling surfaces.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign government sets a hexavalent-chromium content limit for any food. Every credible Cr(VI) instrument on the register is an article, textile, leather, toy-migration, tattoo-ink, fertiliser or electrical-equipment limit in a non-food basis, and applying one to a food matrix would be a basis conflation the compiler's basis guard rejects.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU (Regulation (EU) 2023/915; Regulation (EU) 10/2011; Directive 2009/48/EC; REACH restrictions); UK; Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA; FSANZ Schedule 19; Health Canada; Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 Schedule — none sets a hexavalent-chromium content limit for food.
